```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
# The two tables, and the revenue figures in the text above them, are read when the page is
# rendered, never retyped: the explorer's values from its data file (explorer/grid.js, written by the pipeline), the printed August
# values from data/tab5-vs-printed.csv, and the May rows from the same estimating function,
# score_tab5_cell(), run on the May workbook.
gjs <- grep("^window\\.__GRID__ = ", readLines("explorer/grid.js", warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"),
            value = TRUE)
G <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sub(";\\s*$", "", sub("^window\\.__GRID__ = ", "", gjs)), simplifyVector = FALSE)
keys   <- unlist(G$keys)
dials  <- setNames(G$dials, vapply(G$dials, `[[`, "", "key"))
lev    <- lapply(dials, function(d) unlist(d$levels))
stride <- rev(cumprod(c(1L, rev(lengths(lev))[-length(lev)])))   # first dial slowest
setting <- function(name) setNames(unlist(G$named[[name]]), names(dials))   # 0-based level indices
# One explorer cell: a named setting, with the dials given by value changed.
cell <- function(..., from = setting(G$preferred)) {
  idx <- from; ch <- list(...)
  for (k in names(ch)) {
    j <- which(abs(lev[[k]] - ch[[k]]) < 1e-6); stopifnot(length(j) == 1L); idx[[k]] <- j - 1L
  }
  setNames(unlist(G$snap[[1L + sum(idx * stride)]]), keys)
}
base <- cell()
b0   <- Map(function(l, i) l[i + 1L], lev, setting(G$preferred))   # the base setting's dial values
# round() before formatC(): R's round() gives 103.82 for 103.815, as the report prints it.
f2   <- function(x) { s <- formatC(abs(round(x, 2)), format = "f", digits = 2)
                      ifelse(round(x, 2) < 0, paste0("\u2212", s), s) }
f1   <- function(x) formatC(round(x, 1), format = "f", digits = 1)
pct  <- function(x) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 0), "%")
sw   <- function(k) sprintf("%s (%s)", dials[[k]]$sym, dials[[k]]$label)
tp   <- read.csv("data/tab5-vs-printed.csv")
printed_wt <- function(r) tp$printed[tp$column == "wealth_tax_revenue" & tp$row == r]

# The May workbook (15 April 2026 list), through the same estimating function.
invisible(lapply(list.files("../R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE), source))
may_rev <- withr::with_envvar(c(BSZ_VINTAGE = "may"), {
  inp <- tab5_scoring_inputs(compute_pareto_missing(extract_pareto_missing()),
                             extract_tab2(), extract_tab3())
  stopifnot(inp$vintage == "may")
  c(score_tab5_cell(inp)[["wealth_tax_revenue"]],
    score_tab5_cell(inp, pareto = TRUE)[["wealth_tax_revenue"]],
    score_tab5_cell(inp, leavers = TRUE)[["wealth_tax_revenue"]],
    score_tab5_cell(inp, pareto = TRUE, leavers = TRUE)[["wealth_tax_revenue"]])
})
may_printed <- c(98, 121, 84, 109)   # May 2026 paper, Table 5 rows 1 to 4, PDF p.34

n_added <- cell(from = setting("Missing billionaires"))[["n_billionaires"]] - base[["n_billionaires"]]
checks <- data.frame(
  variation = c("Main assumptions, for reference",
                sprintf("Add the %s billionaires Forbes misses, estimated from the shape of the list",
                        formatC(n_added, format = "f", digits = 0)),
                "Page, Thiel, Hankey and Kalanick escape the tax",
                "Both of the above",
                "Wealth valued on 15 April 2026",
                "15 April, plus the billionaires Forbes misses",
                "15 April, plus the four leavers escape",
                "15 April, plus both"),
  paper   = c(sprintf("Aug, Table 5 row %d", 1:4), sprintf("May, Table 5 row %d", 1:4)),
  printed = c(vapply(1:4, printed_wt, 0), may_printed),
  opa     = c(vapply(names(G$named), function(n) cell(from = setting(n))[["wealth_tax_revenue"]], 0),
              may_rev),
  how     = c("Explorer, as it opens",
              sprintf("Explorer: switch %s on", sw("pareto")),
              sprintf("Explorer: switch %s on", sw("leavers")),
              sprintf("Explorer: switches %s and %s on", dials$pareto$sym, dials$leavers$sym),
              rep("R code, May workbook", 4)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(names(G$named), c("Base", "Missing billionaires", "Leavers", "Missing + leavers")))
checks$result <- ifelse(round(checks$opa) == checks$printed, "Match", "Differs")
n_var   <- nrow(checks) - 1L
n_match <- sum(checks$result[-1] == "Match")
stopifnot(n_var == 7L)   # the word "seven" below
```

`r if (n_match == n_var) "All seven" else paste(n_match, "of the seven")` variations the BSZ papers print reproduce at the paper's rounding. The one assumption
that moves the revenue as much as these, the date on which wealth is valued, cannot be set in
this OPA.

## What was checked

The BSZ paper prints the revenue of the one-time tax, $`r printed_wt(1)` billion, under its main assumptions
(Table 5, row 1). This OPA computes that figure as $`r f1(base[["wealth_tax_revenue"]])` billion. The paper also prints the
revenue under a few other assumptions. Each check below sets the same assumptions in this OPA and
compares the result with the printed figure.

The checks use the wealth tax revenue of Table 5, not this OPA's main estimate of $`r f1(base[["main_estimate"]])` billion.
The main estimate adds income tax effects that the paper does not print under other assumptions,
so there is no printed figure to check it against.

The two versions of the paper (August 2026 and May 2026) print seven such variations, all in
Table 5. The May version values wealth on 15 April 2026 instead of 1 July 2026.

## Results

All figures are in billions of dollars. "Match" means this OPA's value rounds to the printed
figure.

::: {.table-scroll}

```{r}
#| label: checks-table
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
knitr::kable(data.frame(checks$variation, checks$paper, checks$printed, f2(checks$opa),
                        checks$result, checks$how),
             format = "pipe", align = "llrrll",
             col.names = c("Variation", "Paper", "Printed", "This OPA", "Result", "How to set it"))
```

:::

## What could not be checked

**The valuation date.** The authors' workbook gives the revenue for every day of 2026. It is
$92.5 billion on 1 January (the residency date), $87.0 billion at the year's low on 30 March, and
$110.9 billion at its high so far on 6 October. This OPA values wealth on 1 July 2026. The
measure values wealth on 31 December 2026 (BSZ PDF p.23); the BSZ analysis uses the 1 July list,
and this OPA follows it. The only
other date it can use is 15 April, through the May workbook. It has no setting for any other
date, so these three figures cannot be reproduced.

**The explorer's four numeric dials.** The paper prints the revenue at one value of avoidance
(α), of the share of avoidance that is leaving (m), of avoidance by the less visible billionaires
(αₛ) and of the share of the tax paid by selling assets (s). It prints no revenue at any other
value of these four. Moving them in the explorer has no printed figure to compare with.

## Who ran these checks

Claude Code agents chose the variations from the papers and ran the checks on 15 October 2026.
The scripts were then rerun once, in a separate session, with the same results. The author has
not yet reviewed these checks.

To rerun them from the repository root:

```sh
Rscript feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/bsz-sensitivity.R
```

The full record, with the source of every figure, is in
[bsz-sensitivity.md](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/bsz-sensitivity.md).
A second record, [bsz.md](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/feedback/scenario-tests-2026-10-15/bsz.md),
checks ten other numbers the paper prints. Six match and one is close. Three differ: a Table 5
loss cell (the paper's rounding), the revenue-maximising rate (the paper's first-order formula),
and the break-even on page 22. There the paper says that if all billionaires left, the lost
income tax would take 25 years to equal the wealth tax, using its 2023-2025 ratio of income tax
to wealth, 0.2% (abstract, Table 2). Table 5's inputs, the 2019-2025 average tax against
1 July 2026 wealth, give 0.13% and about 38 years.

## Settings the paper does not print

This OPA lets a reader change assumptions the paper holds fixed. The table below lists ten such
changes, each made one at a time from the main assumptions, with the result this OPA gives. The
paper prints no figure for any of them, so they are untested against the authors' own work.

We have sent this table to the original authors, requesting them to test whether they obtain the
same results. We will update the responses here.

All figures are in billions of dollars. Wealth tax revenue, the extra income tax from asset sales
(over five years) and the income tax lost per year are the three result columns of the paper's
Table 5. The income tax lost per year is negative, as Table 5 prints it. The net total is this OPA's main estimate: the wealth tax, plus the extra income tax from
asset sales, minus the present value of the income tax lost to leavers over `r G$facts$pv_years` years (`r paste0(100 * G$facts$pv_rate, "%")` a year).
Each setting can be made in the [explorer](explorer/).

::: {.table-scroll}

```{r}
#| label: settings-table
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
stopifnot(abs(b0$mobility_share - 0.5) < 1e-9, abs(b0$sell_share - 1/3) < 1e-6)   # "half", "one third" below
settings <- list(
  list("None, the main assumptions, for reference", cell()),
  list(sprintf("No avoidance or evasion (%s = 0, instead of %s)", dials$avoidance$sym, pct(b0$avoidance)),
       cell(avoidance = 0)),
  list(sprintf("Avoidance and evasion of %s", pct(0.05)), cell(avoidance = 0.05)),
  list(sprintf("Avoidance and evasion of %s", pct(0.20)), cell(avoidance = 0.20)),
  list(sprintf("Avoidance and evasion of %s", pct(0.30)), cell(avoidance = 0.30)),
  list(sprintf("None of the avoidance is leaving California (%s = 0, instead of half)",
               dials$mobility_share$sym), cell(mobility_share = 0)),
  list(sprintf("All of the avoidance is leaving California (%s = 1)", dials$mobility_share$sym),
       cell(mobility_share = 1)),
  list(sprintf("None of the tax is paid by selling assets (%s = 0, instead of one third)",
               dials$sell_share$sym), cell(sell_share = 0)),
  list(sprintf("All of the tax is paid by selling assets (%s = 1)", dials$sell_share$sym),
       cell(sell_share = 1)),
  list(sprintf("The billionaires Forbes misses are counted, with %s avoidance among them (instead of %s)",
               pct(0.10), pct(b0$avoidance_small)), cell(pareto = 1, avoidance_small = 0.10)),
  list(sprintf("The billionaires Forbes misses are counted, with %s avoidance among them", pct(0.50)),
       cell(pareto = 1, avoidance_small = 0.50)))
v <- function(k) vapply(settings, function(x) x[[2]][[k]], 0)
knitr::kable(data.frame(vapply(settings, `[[`, "", 1),
                        f2(v("wealth_tax_revenue")), f2(v("extra_ca_inctax_sales")),
                        f2(v("annual_ca_inctax_loss")), f2(v("main_estimate")),
                        c("", rep("Pending", length(settings) - 1L))),
             format = "pipe", align = "lrrrrl",
             col.names = c("Setting changed from the main assumptions", "Wealth tax revenue",
                           "Extra income tax from asset sales", "Income tax lost per year",
                           "Net total", "Authors' result"))
```

:::

Both tables are built when this page is rendered, from the explorer's data file
(`site/explorer/grid.js`, which the pipeline writes), so they show the values the explorer shows.
The May rows run the same estimating function on the May workbook.
